title.en: How animals suit their homes (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en:
Jaya saw a camel walking steadily on hot sand. "Why do its feet not sink?" she asked.
"Its feet are wide and flat," said the guide, "like snow shoes for sand. Camels also store fat in their humps for days without food."

Animals live in different places and their bodies suit these places. This is called adaptation.
Desert animals such as camels have wide flat feet for sand, long eyelashes against dust, and can go long without water.
Water animals such as fish have a streamlined body, fins to swim and gills to breathe in water. Ducks have webbed feet.
Birds have wings and light bodies with feathers to fly. Their hollow bones keep them light.
Animals in cold places, such as polar bears, have thick fur and a layer of fat to keep warm.
Every animal's body suits its home. This is adaptation.
A camel has wide feet for sand and can go long without water.
A fish has fins to swim and gills to breathe in water.
A bird has wings and light feathers to fly. A polar bear has thick fur against the cold.

problem.en: Why does a duck have webbed feet?

text.en: Webbed feet work like paddles and push water back.

why.en: They give a bigger surface to push.

text.en: So webbed feet help it swim.

why.en: This is an adaptation to water.

prompt.en: Your friend asks why a polar bear does not feel cold. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: It has thick fur and a layer of fat under the skin.
These adaptations keep its body warm.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the animal does not feel cold because it is strong.

points.en: Adaptation means body features that help living in a habitat.
Camels suit the desert; fish suit water; birds suit the air.
Polar animals have thick fur and fat to stay warm.
